title: Effect of Intermetallic Phases on Tensile Behavior and Mechanical Heterogeneity of AM50 Magnesium Alloy
content: AM50 magnesium alloy is widely considered for lightweight structural and energy-absorbing applications due to its low density, castability, and favorable specific mechanical properties. However, its mechanical response is strongly affected by microstructural heterogeneity, particularly the morphology and distribution of intermetallic constituents formed during casting. In this study, an as-cast AM50 magnesium alloy was investigated by optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, quantitative image analysis, hardness testing, tensile testing, and fractographic examination. The microstructure consisted predominantly of an α-Mg matrix with Al- and Mn-enriched secondary constituents distributed mainly along interdendritic regions and grain boundaries. Quantitative image analysis indicated that the Mg-rich matrix occupied most of the analyzed area, while Al- and Mn-enriched regions represented smaller fractions of the microstructure. Microhardness measurements revealed a pronounced mechanical contrast between the α-Mg matrix and the intermetallic regions, confirming local mechanical heterogeneity. Tensile tests showed an average ultimate tensile strength of 129.42 ± 17.63 MPa and limited ductility, with significant scatter in strain to fracture. Fractographic analysis revealed a mixed ductile–brittle fracture behavior, characterized by dimples, tear ridges, rough fracture regions, and localized brittle features. The results demonstrate that the mechanical performance of as-cast AM50 alloy is controlled not only by the presence of intermetallic phases, but mainly by their morphology, distribution, and interaction with the α-Mg matrix during deformation.
